name: Matrix Elimination
description: You are given an integer $$$k$$$ and a matrix $$$v$$$ with $$$n$$$ rows and $$$m$$$ columns. The element in row $$$i$$$ and column $$$j$$$ is denoted by $$$v_{i,j}$$$. A cell $$$(x, y)$$$ is called a peak if its value is greater than or equal to the sum of the values in all other cells in row $$$x$$$ and column $$$y$$$. Formally, $$$(x, y)$$$ is a peak if $$$$$$ v_{x,y} \ge \sum_{\substack{1 \le i \le n \\i \neq x}} v_{i,y} + \sum_{\substack{1 \le j \le m \\j \neq y}} v_{x,j}. $$$$$$ You may perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero): Choose four integers $$$x_l$$$, $$$x_r$$$, $$$y_l$$$, and $$$y_r$$$ ($$$1 \le x_l \le x_r \le n$$$, $$$1 \le y_l \le y_r \le m$$$). Subtract $$$1$$$ from $$$v_{i,j}$$$ for every $$$x_l \le i \le x_r$$$ and $$$y_l \le j \le y_r$$$. Find the minimum number of operations required to obtain a matrix with at least $$$k$$$ peaks.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n, m \le 10^5$$$, $$$1 \le k \le n \cdot m$$$, $$$n \cdot m \le 10^5$$$) — the number of rows, the number of columns, and the required number of peaks. The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$n$$$ lines contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$v_{i,1}, v_{i,2}, \ldots, v_{i,m}$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le v_{i,j} \le 10^9$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n \cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations required to obtain at least $$$k$$$ peaks. If there is no solution, print a single integer $$$-1$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2248F — Matrix Elimination [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
